Position Overview
Sydney Smile Specialists is a leading dental clinic committed to delivering exceptional dental care, with a strong focus on precision, innovation and patient comfort. Its team comprises highly skilled professionals dedicated to providing high-quality services and ensuring each patient receives personalised and professional care.

On behalf of Sydney Smile Specialists, we are seeking an experienced and skilled Dental Technician to join its team. The Dental Technician will be responsible for producing dental models and appliances, including bleaching trays, orthodontic retainers, custom impression trays, provisional veneer templates and occlusal splints, while maintaining strict infection control, sterilisation and quality standards.

Position Responsibilities and Tasks:

•	Receive, disinfect and prepare dental impressions in accordance with infection-control procedures.
•	Pour, trim, articulate and mount dental models for the construction of dental appliances and restorations.
•	Use thermoforming equipment to produce bleaching trays, orthodontic retainers, custom impression trays, provisional veneer templates and occlusal splints.
•	Construct screw-retained immediate implant crowns in accordance with dentists’ prescriptions and technical specifications.
•	Select and prepare suitable materials for the construction, finishing and polishing of dental appliances.
•	Inspect, adjust and repair dental models, crowns and appliances to ensure accuracy and quality.
•	Disinfect completed dental work and maintain laboratory instruments, equipment and work areas.
•	Maintain laboratory records and quality-control documentation.
•	Keep up to date with developments in dental laboratory materials, techniques and equipment.

Qualifications and Skills:

•	Relevant qualification in Dentistry or Dental Technology.
•	At least 1 year of relevant experience in a similar role.
•	Excellent manual dexterity, precision and attention to detail.
•	Ability to interpret dentists’ prescriptions, impressions and dental specifications.
•	Strong quality-control skills to ensure completed work meets required accuracy, functionality and presentation standards. 

Salary: This is a full-time position with competitive remuneration between $79,500 to $85,000 p.a. plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

  Reasons to Apply - At a Glance  
 
 Meaningful, participant-focused work - play a key role in shaping outcomes for people with disabilities through high-quality, person-centred assessments. 
 Join a growing Federal Government agency with a strong focus on operational excellence and career development.

 Australian Citizenship

As a growing Federal Government agency focused on operational excellence, this role offers a chance to contribute to meaningful initiatives and take your career to the next level. 
   
  Your New Role  
 You will be responsible for: 
 
 Conducting comprehensive support needs assessments by engaging with participants and their representatives to gather detailed, accurate information, ensuring a respectful, trauma-informed and person-centred approach throughout the process. 
 Analysing, interpreting and synthesising complex information and external evidence to develop clear, evidence-based assessments that accurately reflect individual circumstances and inform appropriate support outcomes. 
 Preparing high-quality written assessment reports that are clear, consistent and aligned with legislative and policy frameworks, ensuring decisions are transparent, defensible and uphold ethical standards. 
 Communicating effectively with participants, families and stakeholders across a range of channels, explaining assessment processes and outcomes in a way that is accessible, inclusive and easy to understand. 
 
   
   
  What You Will Need to Succeed  
 The successful applicant will demonstrate: 
 
 A recognised tertiary qualification in an allied health or relevant clinical discipline (such as Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Social Work, Psychology, Nursing or similar), is a requirement for the role. 
 Strong assessment capability and background, with the ability to gather, interpret and synthesise complex information to support clear, evidence-based decision-making. 
 Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to convey complex or sensitive information in a clear, respectful and accessible way across diverse audiences. 
 Sound judgement and problem-solving ability, with experience applying policy and managing risk to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes in a complex environment. 
 
   
  The Logistics  
 
 Contract until December 31st, 2026, with a view of extension or permanency. 
 Full-time & Hybrid working arrangement. 
 Hourly rate of $61.86 + super. 
 Australian Citizenship & tertiary qualification (proof required) is mandatory. 
 Opportunities across QLD, including: Brisbane, Chermside, Ipswich, Maroochydore, Mount Gravatt, Robina & Townsville.

Senior Financial Accountant - Reporting and Transformation  
  Sydney CBD, New South Wales  
  
  About the Company  
  This position sits within the corporate financial accounting team of a large, globally listed professional services group. The company operates across multiple international regions, managing high volume revenue streams and complex entity structures. The Sydney head office maintains a close, collaborative local team culture, supported by an offshore shared services function that handles the transactional processing. The local finance team is currently prioritising process improvement, system updates, and the implementation of new global reporting frameworks across the network.    
  Role Description  
  This is a hands-on financial accounting and technical compliance role for a self motivated professional who can work autonomously. Reporting directly to the Group Financial Controller, you will operate as an individual contributor responsible for general ledger integrity, month end reporting, and audit compliance.  
  The position focuses heavily on core corporate financial accounting, financial statement preparation, and variance analysis. It also provides secondary exposure to new compliance frameworks, including supporting the team with the transition into mandatory Tier 1 sustainability disclosures under the new AASB S2 climate related reporting framework, alongside participating in local finance automation projects.  
  This permanent full time position offers an above market salary package that includes a structured annual performance incentive scheme, benchmarking higher than standard financial compliance roles. The hiring team values long term technical capability, quality of work, and cultural fit.    
  Key Responsibilities  
 
  Financial Reporting and P&Ls  : Prepare the monthly financial reporting, including Profit and Loss reports, Balance Sheets, and reconciliations for allocated group entities.  
  Financial Statements and Consolidations  : Prepare the Annual Financial Statements, including consolidations and Goodwill impairment testing, in accordance with AASB and IFRS standards.  
  General Ledger Integrity  : Maintain the accuracy of the general ledger by preparing and processing monthly general, standing, and reversing journals.  
  Variance Analysis  : Complete detailed Profit and Loss variance analysis and provide financial performance commentary directly to the GFC and divisional directors.  
  Statutory Compliance  : Act as the core technical specialist for IFRS and AASB standards, providing guidance on accounting treatments and working with senior finance leadership to ensure group compliance.  
  AASB S2 and ESG Disclosure  : Coordinate data collection and reporting requirements as required under the new AASB S2 climate disclosure framework.  
  Audit and Internal Controls  : Assist the Assistant GFC with the monthly review of Balance Sheet reconciliations and support the implementation of audit recommendations.  
  Local Collaboration  : Work closely with multiple teams and functions to meet reporting deadlines and provide internal technical assistance where required.  
  Finance Transformation  : Support process improvement, system upgrades, and automation initiatives by utilising modern analytical and AI tools.  
  Templates and Process Improvement  : Create and update financial templates to improve month end reporting efficiency.  
 
 
  Qualifications and Skills  
 
  A Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Finance, Accounting, or a related discipline.  
  CA or CPA qualification is essential  .  
  A background in statutory reporting and core financial accounting.  
  Strong technical proficiency in AASB and IFRS, with an interest in developing exposure to the new AASB S2 climate reporting framework.  
  Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.  
  Demonstrated ability to leverage modern AI tools to efficiently resolve day to day technical accounting challenges.  
  Clear communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with local team members.  
  Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to continuous process improvement.  
 
 
  If you are a highly analytical, execution focused financial accountant looking to step into a global corporate structure, apply now.
